order: Make the review engine selectable through a single configuration key in the project settings file, so the choice of which engine judges a review lives in one place rather than being hardcoded. Support at minimum a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with a fallback to the default when the alternate is unavailable, and a dual mode where both engines review substantively and a coordinating role arbitrates between them. Keep both engines installed under one contract regardless of which is selected, so switching changes only who judges, never what gets checked. Grant the coordinating role a narrow read carve-out for the settings file itself, so it can check the active engine without spending a research step, and make clear this is a permission grant, not a change to any existing guard. Update the review-routing logic to honor the setting and document the key and the swap flow in the project's top-level documentation.
claims: The engine choice was moved into a single configuration key supporting a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with fallback to the default when unavailable, and a dual mode with arbitration. Both engines remain installed under one contract regardless of selection. A narrow read carve-out for the settings file was added to existing role law — read access was never guard-blocked, so this is documented permission, not a guard change — and the review-routing logic and top-level documentation were updated to match, across two files.
